content:
maria: FYI storage bill jumped. Thinking we should compact old token-level events into compact audit envelopes after 90d. Keep full auditability but cut cold storage/scan costs. Thoughts?

oliver: Compacting ok but legal will push on deletions. No raw deletes without hold options.

maria: Not deleting. Plan: keep 90d raw, after that write an envelope per tenant/day/model_family/price_version, include aggregates + deterministic samples + integrity proof. Then reclaim raw shards.

josh: Reprocess concern: can envelopes support deterministic replay for price changes/backfills?

maria: Yes — envelope must be replayable. We store sampling seed, provenance pointers, merkle root. Rehydration path from cold objects with SLA tiers.

sehaj: Implementation idea: compactor grabs partition lease (tenant,bill_date,model), computes merkle_root over original row hashes, writes envelope atomically and emits compaction-finalized event.

infra-bot: (deploy) compactor v0.1 scheduled to run in staging 03:00 UTC.

oliver: SLA: legal asks 30d for some enterprise audits. Propose tiered rehydrate SLAs: enterprise 6h, standard 24h, free best-effort.

josh: Operational risk: overlapping compaction runs. Need idempotent writer and lease checks. Also add coverage metric comparing envelope aggregates vs incremental rollups.

qa-anna: Keep deterministic sample selection and include sample_ids (obj://...) for QA. Also include sample hashes so we detect tampering.

maria: Next steps: prototype envelope schema + merkle lib, small staging run on test tenants, cost delta analysis, RFC for legal/ops signoff. Volunteers?

josh: I'll do prototype tests.

sehaj: I'll own crypto + lease integration.

oliver: I'll coordinate with legal + ops runbook.

qa-anna: QA sampling tests from me.

maria: Thanks — I'll open RFC PR tomorrow with schema and cost numbers.
